title: "File Is Not PDF/X-1a Compliant": How to Fix It (IngramSpark) | SparkPrep
h1: How to fix "your file is not PDF/X-1a compliant"
description: IngramSpark asks for PDF/X-1a print files. Here's why a normal PDF fails, and how to export a compliant one from Word, InDesign, Canva or Acrobat.
lead: Not every PDF is a print PDF. PDF/X-1a is a stricter kind built for printers, and IngramSpark asks for it.
error: The file is not PDF/X-1a compliant
errorNote: Paraphrased. Each printer words this a little differently.
why:
PDF/X-1a is a print standard. It requires CMYK or grayscale color (no RGB), every font embedded, no live transparency, and a note inside the file saying which printing conditions it was made for (the "output intent").

A regular "Save as PDF" from Word or a "PDF Standard" download from Canva doesn't meet those rules, so IngramSpark's checks flag it. Barnes & Noble Press and Lulu also ask for PDF/X-1a files. KDP doesn't require PDF/X-1a, but a PDF/X-1a file works there too.
manual: Convert all color to CMYK (or grayscale for black and white pages) and embed every font.
In InDesign, go to File → Export → Adobe PDF (Print) and pick the "PDF/X-1a:2001" preset. Word can't make PDF/X-1a by itself, so use Acrobat Pro: Print Production → Preflight → "Convert to PDF/X-1a".
Run Acrobat's Preflight to confirm the file is PDF/X-1a compliant.
Re-upload it to your printer and wait for the file review again. If it fails, you start over.

faq.a: IngramSpark asks for PDF/X-1a:2001 files. It's the safest format to send them.
